name: Question 2
problem:
Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).$

$\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,\frac{32{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯$
worked_solution:
The Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $4x$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x) & =(4x)-\frac{(4x)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(4x)^{5}}{5!}-⋯ \\  & =4x-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{6}+\frac{1024{x}^{5}}{120}-⋯ \\  & =4x-\frac{32{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{256{x}^{5}}{30}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

The Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $2x$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & =1-\frac{(2x)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(2x)^{4}}{24}-⋯ \\  & =1-2{x}^{2}+\frac{16{x}^{4}}{24}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the expansions for $\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & =(4x-\frac{32{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{256{x}^{5}}{30}-⋯)+(1-2{x}^{2}+\frac{16{x}^{4}}{24}-⋯) \\  & =1+4x-2{x}^{2}-\frac{32{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The Maclaurin expansion of sin⁡(x) is sin⁡(x)=x−x33!+x55!−⋯.

Replacing x with 4x we get sin⁡(4x)=(4x)−(4x)33!+(4x)55!−⋯=4x−64x36+1024x5120−⋯=4x−32x33+256x530−⋯.

The Maclaurin expansion of cos⁡x is cos⁡x=1−x22!+x44!−⋯.

Replacing x with 2x we get cos⁡(2x)=1−(2x)22+(2x)424−⋯=1−2x2+16x424−⋯.

Adding the expansions for sin⁡(4x) and cos⁡(2x), we get sin⁡(4x)+cos⁡(2x)=(4x−32x33+256x530−⋯)+(1−2x2+16x424−⋯)=1+4x−2x2−32x33+⋯.
